- When sentiment shows strong positive momentum (e.g., recent sentiment change > 0.5) and model overestimates, reduce forecast slightly to avoid overshoot.  
- If sentiment turns negative or shows sharp decline (e.g., sentiment change < -0.5), model tends to overcorrect — lower forecast by 1–2% to align with mean reversion.  
- Model often lags behind true price movements in early days of a new trend — adjust forecast upward by 0.5–1.5% for the first 3–5 days of a sentiment shift.  
- When news volume is high and sentiment is volatile, model tends to overreact — apply a dampening factor (e.g., reduce forecast by 0.3–0.7% per 1.0 sentiment change).  
- For 30-day horizon, if true outcome shows strong downward trend after a spike, model often fails to recognize mean reversion — reduce forecast by 1–3% in the 10–15 day window post-spike.  
- If sentiment is flat or neutral (last 3 sentiment changes near 0), model tends to overpredict — reduce forecast by 0.5–1.0% to avoid false momentum.
